dual_writer_resolution: RESOLVED. The round-1 CONFLICT-RISK (grants.ts carrying a LOCAL partial/non-JCS preimage writer — SHA-256(prevHash || type || actor || subject || occurred_at) — on the same vocab=1 audit_event/audit_head tables) is fixed. The local chain math is DELETED from src/http/grants.ts (grep for createHash/prevHash/rowHash/sha256 → 0 hits; the prior fed338a version had createHash + manual seq/prev_hash/row_hash + audit_head upsert — all gone). grants.ts now appends through the canonical sink: grantAuditWriter = makePgAuditWriter(); appendAuditEventInput → grantAuditWriter.appendAuditEvent(client, input). writeGrant/writeAssignmentAuditEvent encode via the T-0031 encoders then route through the single writer, inside the caller's withTenantTx (tx-semantics preserved). The audit_writer_isolation.sh fitness check ENFORCES this chokepoint: it greps for INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on choros.audit_(event|head) outside src/db/audit-writer.ts. NEGATIVE PROOF: reviewer injected a rogue `INSERT INTO choros.audit_event` literal into grants.ts → check exits 1 ('audit write-SQL found outside src/db/audit-writer.ts: .../grants.ts'); reverted → exit 0. The mixed grant+lifecycle interleaved chain is covered live (audit-writer.chain.test.ts, isolated DB): dense +1 chain under one vocab + tamper-detect on a grant row via the SAME canonical recompute as the lifecycle row — no dual preimage. One sink, one preimage, verifiable interleaved chain.
instance_started_assessment: HONEST FORWARD — NOT an AC-dyra; acceptable against the spec. Reviewer independently confirmed there is NO production call-site for flowableClient.startInstance anywhere in src (grep: startInstance appears only as the FlowableClient method DEFINITION in src/core/flowable-client.ts and is invoked only by flowable-client.* tests — no HTTP route, no server.ts call, no process emits an instance-start today). FR-3's trigger ('successful startInstance') therefore has no upstream producer in this build — you cannot audit an event no production code emits, and starting an instance is a downstream concern outside T-0068's audit-projection scope. AC-7 is verifiable_as:'test' (the spec does NOT require live-DB for it), and it IS met: auditInstanceStarted is the sanctioned wrapper, unit-covered via the in-memory writer, and the ADR §4.4/§9 name it as the forward-obligation call-site the future start-instance route MUST invoke (on ok:true inside its own withTenant tx). Crucially the round-1 R-1 grievance was about the task.completed/task.failed runtime path being dead — that path CAN fire today (outbox dispatcher) and is now live-wired and mutation-proven; instance.started is the one branch honestly inert because its producer is absent in prod. The coder documented this transparently (commit body + ADR §4.4 'Forward-obligation (честный шов): прод-HTTP-route старта инстанса сегодня НЕ существует'), did NOT dress it as live, and did NOT ship a silent uncalled wrapper passed off as wired. This is the right disposition under the integration-honesty gate (D-056): claim narrowed to what is delivered, gap named as a forward-obligation. Adjudicated: ACCEPT.
acceptance_notes: Round-1 marked AC-7/AC-8/AC-14 not-covered because the wired entry point exercised no runtime path. Now flipped to covered: AC-14 — startMain (main.ts) is the composition root, index.ts delegates, startLifecycleBridge registers the dispatcher loop with onDispatched=auditOnDispatched AND the poll loop, degrades no-throw without env (lifecycle-bridge.test.ts FF-9 + main-wired-entry.test.ts both green; createServer verified loop-free). AC-8 (task.completed/task.failed → 1 audit row) — now live end-to-end through the real composition (wired-entry test reddens if the wiring breaks, mutation-proven). AC-7 (instance.started → 1 audit row) — covered at the AC's required level (test / in-memory writer + wrapper); the start-instance route is an explicit named forward-obligation (ADR §4.4/§9), not a T-0068 deliverable, since no production producer of instance-start exists yet (see instance_started_assessment).
role_gap_evidence: D-056 integration-honesty gate proved its worth across BOTH rounds: round-1 it caught a unit-green+fitness-green seam wired by a dep-less call + void-ed callback (the BUILD asserted wiring it did not deliver); round-2 the FIX is itself defended by a mutation-resistant wired-entry test (removing the composition link reddens it) + a negative isolation test (rogue audit INSERT reddens the chokepoint check). The evidence stands: BUILD phase benefits from a 'does the wired entry point actually exercise the new path' self-check before handoff, and the reviewer should mutation-probe wiring claims rather than trust unit-green — both done here.
